statement.text:
We define the class of hierarchically decomposable groups in the following
way. First, if X is any class of groups, then let H1 X denote the class of groups which
admit an admissible action on a finite-dimensional contractible complex in such a way
that every cell stabilizer belongs to X. Then the “big” class HX is defined to be the
smallest H1 -closed class containing X.
   ∗ a) Let F be the class of all finite groups. Find an example of an HF group which
is not in H3 F (= H1 H1 H1 F ).
    b) Prove or disprove that there is an ordinal α such that Hα F = HF, where Hα is
the operator on classes of groups defined by transfinite induction in the obvious way
starting from H1 . Editor’s comment: It is proved that such an ordinal cannot be
countable (T. Januszkiewicz, P. H. Kropholler, I. J. Leary, Bull. London Math. Soc.,
42, No. 5 (2010), 896–904).                                                P. Kropholler
  ∗ a) Such an example is found; moreover, for any countable ordinal α there are
groups in Hα+1 F that are not in Hα F (T. Januszkiewicz, P. H. Kropholler, I. J. Leary,
Bull. London Math. Soc., 42, No. 5 (2010), 896–904). Furthermore, torsion-free
examples with similar properies have been constructed (F. Fournier-Facio, B. Sun,
Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01987v3).
